messages:
Aisha: Quick intake — customer AcmeHealth asked for per-tenant rollout guardrails for model changes (regulated data). Problem: current global rollouts can cause tenant-specific quality regressions and they need deterministic acceptance before traffic shift.
Tom (Eng): +1. Need to know whether this is a blocking enterprise requirement vs nice-to-have.
Aisha: It's blocking for their Dedicated contract renewal. They want automatic hold if a tenant's eval drops.
Priya: From design POV, we should show clear pass/fail state in Console + explanation. Keep UX minimal: one button to approve per-tenant after checks.
Jen (CS): They also want audit logs of evaluation inputs used and explicit consent flag for customer-supplied eval sets.
Eva (Research): Proposed acceptance metric: run tenant eval suite (N=50 prompts) against new vs baseline; require both: (1) mean preference score >= 0.72, (2) no more than 6 prompts with >30% drop in relevance. We can compute preference via pairwise preference model.
Tom (Eng): Feasible. Questions: where do evals run (hosted vs customer infra)? If on Redwood hosted, data residency concerns for AcmeHealth.
Aisha: They want evals inside their VPC (Private deployment). For Dedicated, evals can run on reserved infra. Ops constraints: must support both.
ops-bot: Note: creating RFC ticket #INF-2147 and pipeline feature flag `tenant_acceptance_gate`.
Tom (Eng): Technical acceptance checklist (draft):
```
- gate_enabled: boolean
- eval_source: [tenant, redwood_shared]
- eval_count: int (default 50)
- pass_threshold: 0.72
- regression_limit: 6
- auto_rollout_on_pass: boolean
- rollback_on_postroll_drop_pct: 5
```
Priya: UX acceptance: console shows per-tenant status, link to the 50-sample diff report, timestamped approvals, and a single CTA to "Approve rollout" or "Hold and Investigate". Minimal drilldown for non-tech reviewers.
Jen (CS): Customer asks — must support scheduled rolling windows (e.g., only test during low-traffic hours) and notification to their SRE Slack channel.
Aisha: Non-goals: we will not build automated prompt-level fixes or model retuning in phase 1. Also no cross-tenant aggregation for acceptance (each tenant evaluated independently).
Eva (Research): Edge cases to consider: small tenants (<200 monthly requests) — sample size too small. Proposal: require a fallback mechanism: if tenant_eval_count < 10, mark manual review required.
Tom (Eng): Implementation notes: integrate with rollout service, run evals as shaded traffic (1% mirrored) or offline against stored samples. For Private deployments, provide an agent that runs evals inside customer network and returns metrics only.
Aisha: Success metrics (v1):
- 95% of regulated tenants have automated acceptance enabled within 30 days of feature GA
- Zero production-quality regressions for gated tenants on rollout (monitored via post-rollout quality alerts)
- Time-to-decision for a tenant (eval run + report) <= 20 minutes for typical eval_count=50
Tom (Eng): Perf targets: p95 eval latency < 15 min for large models (we'll parallelize). Cost target: average cost per tenant eval run < $10 for common models; justify if above.
Priya: Launch criteria: engineering implementation merged + console UI + on-prem agent + runbook + one pilot customer (AcmeHealth) signed off.
Jen (CS): Rollout plan: pilot with AcmeHealth, then open to Dedicated customers by request, GA after 8 weeks of piloting and stability checks.
Aisha: Asks: @Tom can you rough-estimate engineering effort (sprint count)? @Eva can you validate evaluation thresholds with a small offline analysis? @Priya can you mock the console states for review?
Tom (Eng): I'll scoped it as ~3 sprints (backend + agent + infra), + 1 sprint for integrations. Need a follow-up RFC for api surface.
Eva (Research): I'll run offline sims on 10 tenant datasets and report recommended thresholds tomorrow.
Priya: I'll post 3 mock states by EOD.
Jen (CS): I'll coordinate pilot kickoff and customer requirements doc.
Aisha: Great — next step: I'll open the RFC and attach this thread. Please add any missing edge cases here. :raised_hands:
